correctness.rationale: The Rademacher cross terms from distinct unordered pairs are orthogonal, so the variance is four times the sum of G_ij² over monochromatic unordered pairs (equivalently twice the ordered sum). The homogeneous left and right solutions are strictly monotone by induction with positive killing; the interior equations conserve the conductance-weighted Wronskian. The piecewise product solves each inverse column: the single diagonal jump, including the one-sided endpoint cases, contributes precisely that Wronskian. Squaring the product and telescoping both positive increments gives the interval kernel, including its boundary coefficients. Each interval count-square sum is minimized by balanced counts, and residues balance every interval at once. Equality forces each length-k window to have all colors, hence entering and departing colors agree; k=1 is trivial, and k=n consists of singletons. A collision in a length-k window costs at least two count-square units, giving the stated factor four. Independent bounded replay: python /workspace/replay/checks.py 2 constructs a new rational five-site matrix, computes exact variances by averaging over all sign vectors, and checks interval gaps and k! labeled optima for each budget. It is a normalization and uniqueness check on that instance, not the proof for all paths.
